pages.text: A true edge opens a cut that does not close on its own. A point is not the same as an edge; a stick that is merely sharp will not do it.$(br2)A cut animal runs. Let it.

You are not faster than it. You do not need to be.$(br2)Stay close. Keep following. An animal that cannot shake you will slow, and then stop.$(br2)This is the oldest hunting there is, and it is won by the one who does not give up.

Anything you strike bolts, unless it is the sort of thing that comes back at you. It gets a hard sprint you cannot follow, then settles into a longer run - and everything grazing beside it runs too.$(br2)You cannot win the sprint. You win the afternoon: it overheats and you sweat, and a wound that keeps opening will not close for three minutes.

From habilis, think ($(k:hominin_evolution.think)) once the animal has run, and you hold the shape of it and the ground it went over - it is marked for its first run.$(br2)Erectus can do this again whenever the mark fades, as often as it takes, but each time costs water. Carry some.$(br2)This is for animals big enough to outrun you. Before habilis, take what small things you can catch.
